newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury official urges backing for IMF.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury official urges backing for IMF.

text.p: A senior Treasury Department official told Congress on Thursday the best way to guarantee reform of the International Monetary Fund was for the United States to back it financially.

"Ability to press successfully for continued reforms in the IMF depends upon our demonstrating that our commitment to the institution is as strong now as it was when we spearheaded its creation 50 years ago," said Timothy Geithner, senior deputy assistant Treasury secretary for international affairs.
Treasury issued a copy of Geithner's testimony for the House banking subcommittee on international monetary policy.
Geithner said the Clinton administration also was reviewing the adequacy of IMF quota payments and said it might propose that Congress boost the U.S. contribution.

"We will consult closely with Congress as this review proceeds," he said. The IMF is "critically important" to the United States because of the rapid increase in financial integration around the world and because of changing international capital markets, Geithner said.
